description: Organizes a contract dispute into logically dependent questions so that formation, terms, performance, defenses, and remedies are addressed in the correct order.
application_scenario: Use when a case contains several connected claims, counterclaims, or alternative legal characterizations arising from the same transaction or course of dealings.
reasoning_flow: Identify each distinct claim, defense, counterclaim, and requested remedy.
Group the questions into formation, party identity, terms, performance, breach, excuse, causation, and remedy.
Mark prerequisite relationships, such as a payment claim depending on contractual entitlement or a remedy depending on an established breach.
Resolve common factual predicates once and carry them consistently into all dependent issues.
Separate alternative routes to relief and identify which later questions become unnecessary after an earlier determination.
Combine the issue-level determinations into a coherent disposition without double counting liability or loss.
example_application: A supplier seeks an unpaid balance while the customer alleges delay, defects, and additional expense. The template first establishes the agreement and its terms, then evaluates reciprocal performance, cross-claims, and the net remedial position.

template_name: Contract Formation from Communications and Conduct
description: Determines whether the parties reached a binding agreement when assent is disputed or must be inferred from conversations, documents, performance, and surrounding conduct.
application_scenario: Use for alleged oral agreements, informal commercial arrangements, unsigned terms, preliminary negotiations, or transactions completed through conduct rather than one formal instrument.
reasoning_flow: Identify the alleged offer, acceptance, consideration, and intended contracting parties.
Reconstruct the sequence of communications and conduct at the time agreement was allegedly reached.
Distinguish concluded terms from negotiations, provisional understandings, and agreements subject to further approval or documentation.
Test whether the essential terms are sufficiently certain and whether the parties objectively intended immediate legal commitment.
Check whether later performance, invoicing, payment, or reliance confirms or contradicts the alleged agreement.
State the contract, if any, at the level of terms actually established by the evidence.
example_application: One party claims that a fee arrangement was agreed during meetings, while the other says discussions remained preliminary. The analysis compares the contemporaneous communications, subsequent assistance, invoicing, and the certainty of the alleged fee term.

template_name: Contracting Party, Agency, and Privity Alignment
description: Identifies who acquired contractual rights and obligations when agents, related entities, intermediaries, nominees, or replacement performers participated in the transaction.
application_scenario: Use when a person negotiated on behalf of another, an intermediary issued documents or collected payment, a related company performed work, or one party allegedly replaced another.
reasoning_flow: List every person or entity involved in negotiation, signature, performance, payment, documentation, and receipt of benefits.
Identify any express or implied authority and distinguish agent, principal, subcontractor, assignee, nominee, and independent contracting party roles.
Examine how the parties were described in operative documents and how they represented their roles to each other.
Determine whether later conduct created substitution, assignment, novation, ratification, or merely administrative assistance.
Match each contractual right, duty, and remedy to the legally relevant party.
Consider non-contractual liability separately where privity is absent but an independent duty may exist.
example_application: A service provider performs through a related entity that issues invoices and receives payment. The template determines whether that entity became the contracting party or merely acted for the original provider.

description: Reconstructs the operative contract where obligations are distributed across preliminary agreements, formal documents, supplemental writings, guarantees, correspondence, and oral arrangements.
application_scenario: Use when multiple instruments overlap, a later document may preserve or replace earlier terms, or the parties dispute whether an ancillary writing changed the original bargain.
reasoning_flow: Collect the documents and communications said to contain or modify contractual terms.
Order them chronologically and identify the transaction or obligation addressed by each.
Determine whether each instrument incorporates, supplements, varies, supersedes, settles, or merely records an existing obligation.
Resolve inconsistencies using the text, commercial context, and the parties' subsequent implementation.
Identify any terms that survive execution of a later formal document and any obligations displaced by it.
Produce one consolidated statement of the operative terms relevant to the disputed issues.
example_application: A provisional agreement is followed by draft formal terms and later correspondence. The analysis determines which obligations were immediately binding, which depended on a later instrument, and whether any preliminary term survived.

description: Classifies disputed obligations and determines when performance, payment, rejection, termination, or another consequence becomes due.
application_scenario: Use when liability depends on a condition precedent, approval, certification, completion milestone, notice requirement, time stipulation, or distinction between a condition and a lesser term.
reasoning_flow: Identify the event or act said to trigger the disputed obligation or remedy.
Interpret the relevant wording in the context of the contract as a whole and its commercial function.
Classify the term as a condition precedent, condition, warranty, intermediate term, timing provision, or administrative step.
Determine whether strict, substantial, or reasonable compliance is required.
Assess whether the trigger occurred, was waived, prevented, or became impossible through either party's conduct.
Apply the consequence attached to the proper classification without extending it beyond the contract.
example_application: Payment is said to depend on completion, approval, or execution of a further document. The template determines the legal character of that requirement and whether the necessary trigger occurred.

template_name: Conformity, Defect, and Substantial Performance Assessment
description: Evaluates whether goods, works, or services conformed to the promised description, sample, specification, quality, and functional requirements.
application_scenario: Use for defective goods, faulty workmanship, incomplete systems, nonconforming materials, failed repairs, or disputes over whether defects justify rejection, withholding payment, or damages.
reasoning_flow: Translate contractual descriptions, samples, specifications, and functional promises into verifiable performance criteria.
Compare the delivered goods, work, or service with each criterion using inspections, records, expert evidence, and admissions.
Distinguish patent defects, latent defects, incomplete items, and deviations accepted or approved during performance.
Assess the seriousness of each defect and whether overall performance was substantial.
Determine whether notice, opportunity to inspect, acceptance, use, or attempted cure affects the available response.
Match the established nonconformity to the proper consequence, such as cure, price adjustment, damages, withholding, or rejection.
example_application: A contractor claims the balance of the price, while the customer alleges poor workmanship and unfinished corrective work. The analysis measures the work against the agreed requirements and distinguishes remediable defects from failures going to the substance of performance.

template_name: Reciprocal Performance, Prevention, and Default Sequence
description: Determines responsibility where each side alleges that the other's delay, omission, or refusal prevented or excused its own performance.
application_scenario: Use in staged contracts, construction or supply arrangements, transactions requiring cooperation, and disputes involving late inputs, withheld payment, missing approvals, or mutual failure by a deadline.
reasoning_flow: Place each reciprocal obligation and contractual deadline on a single performance timeline.
Identify dependencies, including information, access, materials, payment, approval, and cooperation required from the other side.
Assess whether each party was ready, willing, and able to perform when its obligation arose.
Determine whether one party caused, materially contributed to, or waived the event relied on as the other's default.
Separate independent breaches from failures excused by prevention, prior breach, agreed extension, or concurrent default.
Allocate the legal and financial consequences according to the established sequence of responsibility.
example_application: A manufacturer alleges late delivery of materials, while the buyer alleges late production and withholds payment. The template reconstructs the sequence and determines which failures were independent and which were caused by the other party.

template_name: Variation, Waiver, Settlement, and Termination Effect
description: Determines how later agreements or conduct changed, suspended, settled, or ended the parties' original contractual rights.
application_scenario: Use when the parties signed a supplemental arrangement, accepted altered performance, agreed a reduced sum, mutually terminated, settled outstanding accounts, or disputed the effect of post-breach conduct.
reasoning_flow: Identify the original rights and obligations immediately before the alleged change or termination.
Specify the later words, document, payment, or conduct relied on as variation, waiver, settlement, mutual termination, or election.
Test whether the alleged change was sufficiently certain, authorized, communicated, and supported by any legally required form or consideration.
Determine the scope and duration of the change, including whether rights were permanently released or only suspended.
Check whether later conduct affirmed, revoked, or contradicted the asserted arrangement.
Recalculate the parties' surviving obligations and remedies under the modified legal relationship.
example_application: After disputes over incomplete work, the parties sign a later agreement fixing an amount and allocating corrective obligations. The template determines whether that arrangement settled earlier claims or merely adjusted ongoing performance.

template_name: Misrepresentation, Knowledge, and Contractual Risk Allocation
description: Evaluates whether a false statement induced the transaction and whether knowledge, reliance, disclaimers, exclusion clauses, or later agreements alter responsibility.
application_scenario: Use when a party alleges false documents, inaccurate descriptions, assurances about goods or property, future-oriented statements, or concealment of a known defect or irregularity.
reasoning_flow: Identify each alleged representation, its maker, recipient, timing, and precise factual content.
Classify the statement as fact, opinion, intention, prediction, contractual term, or silence coupled with a duty to disclose.
Determine falsity, the representor's state of mind where relevant, and the recipient's actual reliance or inducement.
Examine the recipient's knowledge, inspection, sophistication, and any later document addressing the same risk.
Interpret any disclaimer, exclusion, non-reliance clause, or contractual allocation of responsibility and test its legal effectiveness.
Determine the compatible remedies and avoid duplicating recovery across contractual and misrepresentation routes.
example_application: A buyer alleges that a product or property was materially misdescribed, while the seller relies on inspection and an exclusion clause. The analysis tests the statement, reliance, knowledge, and the effectiveness of the contractual risk allocation.

template_name: Payment Account, Set-Off, and Net Balance Reconciliation
description: Calculates the legally recoverable balance when payment claims are contested by credits, expenses, defects, deposits, profit-sharing adjustments, or counterclaims.
application_scenario: Use for unpaid invoices, contract balances, partnership or cooperation accounts, reimbursement disputes, margin debts, rent arrears, and claims involving competing monetary adjustments.
reasoning_flow: Identify the contractual or legal basis of every claimed debit and credit.
Separate admitted amounts from disputed charges and link each disputed item to its authorizing term or evidential record.
Verify performance milestones, invoices, statements, receipts, payments, deposits, deductions, and agreed sharing ratios.
Assess whether each asserted set-off or counterclaim is legally available and sufficiently connected to the payment claim.
Exclude unsupported, duplicated, premature, or contractually allocated costs.
Compute the net balance only after resolving the underlying entitlement to each component, then address interest and costs separately.
example_application: A party claims unpaid fees, while the other relies on defective work, prior payments, and expenses charged to the account. The template validates each component before calculating the net amount.

template_name: Illegality and Regulatory Constraint on Enforcement
description: Determines whether performance or enforcement of an otherwise established agreement is restricted by statute, regulation, licensing rules, or public policy.
application_scenario: Use when payment, transfer, professional conduct, property use, corporate action, or another promised act may contravene a regulatory prohibition or depend on official authorization.
reasoning_flow: Identify the contractual obligation whose performance or enforcement is challenged.
Identify the regulatory rule, protected purpose, prohibited conduct, and persons to whom it applies.
Determine whether the contract requires unlawful performance, merely creates a risk of noncompliance, or can be performed lawfully.
Assess the parties' knowledge, responsibility, and any required approval, licence, disclosure, or certification.
Consider severability, restitution, alternative lawful performance, and the effect of the regulatory purpose on private remedies.
Integrate the regulatory determination with the otherwise established contractual rights.
example_application: A party proves a fee arrangement, but payment is alleged to violate a statutory restriction. The template distinguishes formation from enforceability and tests whether the obligation can lawfully be performed.

template_name: Coordinated Contract and Non-Contract Remedy Selection
description: Selects and coordinates remedies where the same facts may support debt, damages, restitution, rescission, rectification, equitable relief, or an independent tort claim.
application_scenario: Use when a dispute combines payment claims with return of deposits, compensation for defects or reliance loss, correction of documents, proprietary relief, injunctions, or negligence and misrepresentation allegations.
reasoning_flow: Match each established wrong or entitlement to its available remedial routes.
Identify prerequisites for each remedy, including termination, causation, proof of loss, inadequacy of damages, restoration, and discretionary factors.
Distinguish expectation, reliance, restitutionary, proprietary, and corrective relief.
Check compatibility, election requirements, mitigation, remoteness, contributory responsibility, and bars to equitable relief.
Prevent duplicate compensation where several causes of action address the same loss.
Sequence monetary and non-monetary orders so that the combined remedy is practically coherent.
example_application: A buyer seeks return of a deposit, damages for misrepresentation, and correction or unwinding of transaction documents. The template evaluates each route and combines only compatible relief without duplicate recovery.
